salicylic acid, c-GMP analog, okadatic acid, IBMX dipyridamol, and glutamate significantly enhanced BDNF production.
salicycic acid, cGMR analog, okada acid, IBMX dipyridamol and glutamate promote the production of BDFN in DA neurons.
salicycic acid, cGmp analog, okadaid acid, IBMX dipyridamol and glutamate significantly increase the production of brain-derived neurotrophic factore in nigral dopamergic neuronal cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of compounds that can promote BDNF production and thereby enhance the survival of DA neuronal cells.
the identification of potential compounds that can be used to promote the production of BNF in DA neurons.
identifying low mol. wt compounds that could potentially be used to enhance the production of BDFN in the DA neuronal cells to prevent their degeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these compounds may promote BDNF production and may be useful as potential drugs for PD.

the compounds tested can increase the production of endogenous BDNF in nigral dopaminerergic neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
these low mol. wt compounds may be potential candidates for the development of neuroprotective drugs for the treatment of PD.

BDNF production can be enhanced in DA neuronal cells by compounds that are known to promote the activity of protein phosphatase 1 (PP1), protein kinase A (PKA), protein kinase C (PKC), cGMP-dependent kinase, and/or adenosine receptor.
BDNF production could be promoted in nigral dopami-nergic neurons by a number of low mol. wt compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a number of compounds that can be used to enhance BDNF levels in the nigral DA neurons.
the nigral DA neurons can produce their own BDNF and that this production can be enhanced with the use of low mol. wt compounds.
these identified compounds could potentially be used as therapeutic agents for PD.
